active_paradigms.idea: Use scipy.optimize.linprog to solve an LP-based lower-bound relaxation (SOS/first-order distance linearization) of the max-min distance NLP, iterating successive LP approximations (Sequential LP / cutting-plane) on the 42+1 variables.
active_paradigms.description: Reformulate maximize t s.t. |pi-pj|^2 >= t, |pi-pj|^2 <= 1. At each iteration linearize the quadratic constraints around the current point (Taylor expansion of squared distances), solve the resulting LP with scipy.optimize.linprog (HiGHS) to get a new candidate, add a trust region to keep linearization valid, and shrink the trust region as convergence is approached. This is a sequential linear programming (SLP) loop: it never uses minimize, converges to KKT points of the exact NLP, and HiGHS is extremely fast so hundreds of restarts from random seeds fit the timeout. Start from the current best configuration and from many random/perturbed seeds, keep the best true (dmin/dmax)^2. The trust-region SLP handles the nonconvex constraints better than soft-min smoothing because each LP is solved to global optimality of the linearization.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: primary score (dmin/dmax)^2 via exact KKT convergence of the constrained NLP
active_paradigms.cautions: Linearization of nonconvex quadratic constraints can diverge; enforce a trust region (bound on ||x - x_k||_inf) and backtrack if the true ratio decreases. Recompute all 91 pair constraints each iteration. Verify final ratio with pdist.

active_paradigms.idea: Use scipy.optimize.root (Newton on the KKT system) to find exact stationary configurations of the max-min problem with active-set identification, exploiting the known optimal 14-point structure (two points at diameter ends + 12 on a ring/antiprism).
active_paradigms.description: The optimal 14-point packing in a unit-diameter ball is believed to have the structure: 2 antipodal cap points and 12 points arranged with dihedral symmetry. Parametrize the configuration by a small number of free parameters (cap positions, ring radius, ring height, ring twist angle, and per-point deviations), identify the active constraint set (pairs at distance exactly t and pairs at diameter 1), and solve the resulting square system of stationarity equations with scipy.optimize.root (hybr/lm). This finds exact algebraic solutions rather than slowly-converging gradient descents, and can be run over a family of symmetry hypotheses (antiprism, twisted ring, capped icosahedron variants). After root-finding, verify and polish with the existing push_polish only if it strictly improves.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: exact stationary points of the constrained NLP, targeting ratios above the reference 1/4.1658
active_paradigms.cautions: The active set must be guessed correctly; try multiple active-set hypotheses generated from the current best configuration's near-degenerate pairs. Root may not converge — wrap in try/except and keep the best verified configuration. Ensure the final array is finite and shape (14,3).

active_paradigms.idea: Use scipy.spatial.ConvexHull-based extreme-point restarts combined with a deterministic coordinate-descent sweep that alternates optimizing each single point against all others (a Voronoi/Lloyd-like max-min step solved per point in closed form via local 1D line search with numpy only).
active_paradigms.description: Instead of joint optimization over 42 variables, use cyclic coordinate optimization: for each point i, its best position (maximizing its min distance to the other 13 while keeping all pairwise distances <= 1) lies along the direction away from its nearest neighbors; perform a per-point 1D golden-section line search (numpy, no scipy.minimize) along the gradient of min-distance-to-others, with a diameter-feasibility projection (rescale if any distance exceeds 1). Sweep points repeatedly until no improvement. Generate restarts from convex hull vertices of random samples and from structured seeds (icosahedron + caps, antiprism), and exploit symmetry: after each sweep, re-symmetrize candidate configurations by averaging over detected symmetric orbits to funnel toward high-symmetry optima. This is fundamentally different: per-point closed-form-ish updates with symmetry projection, no global NLP solver.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: dmin/dmax via greedy per-point repositioning with symmetry funneling
active_paradigms.cautions: Per-point moves must respect the diameter constraint — clamp line-search upper bound so no distance exceeds dmax. Symmetry averaging can hurt if the true optimum is asymmetric; accept only if the true ratio improves. Keep fixed seed, budget sweeps to stay within timeout.

tried_paradigms.idea: Exploit the known optimal 14-point 'hexagonal antiprism + caps' structure and refine it with exact constrained optimization
tried_paradigms.description: The best-known 14-point diameter/distance configurations in 3D are related to icosahedral or antiprismatic symmetry. Instead of random multi-start, directly construct the 14-point configuration as a hexagonal antiprism (12 points) plus 2 polar points on the symmetry axis, parametrized by only 2–3 variables (antiprism radius, height, polar point offset). Sweep or optimize this tiny parametric family exactly with scipy.optimize.minimize (SLSQP) on the exact min-max formulation. This drastically reduces the search space and lands directly at or beyond the known reference ratio. Then finish with the existing exact constrained polish (maximize t s.t. pairwise squared distances in [t^2, 1]) to squeeze the last digits.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Parametrize antiprism with correct twist angle (30 degrees between hexagon layers); also try pentagonal/pentagonal-cap variants and the icosahedron-plus-2 variant; use analytic Jacobians for the SLSQP constraints; verify dmax normalization at the end.

tried_paradigms.idea: Symmetry-restricted optimization: optimize points constrained to a symmetric orbit of a finite rotation group (tetrahedral/octahedral/icosahedral)
tried_paradigms.description: Represent the 14 points as the union of orbits under a point group: e.g., icosahedral group orbits of sizes (12+2), (12+1+1), or octahedral orbits (6+8), (6+6+2). Each orbit is generated from a single free point by applying the group's rotation matrices, so the full 42-dimensional problem collapses to a handful of parameters. Enumerate candidate orbit decompositions summing to 14, optimize the few free parameters with a coarse grid followed by Nelder–Mead or L-BFGS-B on the exact ratio objective, and keep the best. Symmetric configurations provably have many equal pairwise distances, which is the hallmark of optimal min-max configurations and makes the ratio robust to local perturbations.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: primary score via structured, low-dimensional search that avoids poor local optima
tried_paradigms.cautions: Build rotation matrices for each group exactly (use quaternion or matrix generators); orbits may coincide if the base point lies on a symmetry axis — check orbit sizes; after optimization, optionally break symmetry slightly and re-polish with the exact constrained solver since the true optimum may be only near-symmetric.

tried_paradigms.idea: Repulsion-based dynamical simulation: gradient flow on a sum of inverse-power potentials with adaptive diameter normalization
tried_paradigms.description: Run a physically motivated relaxation: place 14 points randomly on the unit sphere and integrate a gradient descent on the energy sum over pairs of 1/d^p (p ~ 6–12), while every step rescaling so the diameter stays 1 (project the farthest pair inward slightly or rescale all points by 1/dmax). Use scipy.integrate.solve_ivp with the analytic gradient, or plain fixed-step gradient descent with adaptive step. Gradually anneal p from 2 up to 20 so that the smallest distances dominate, which drives dmin upward while the diameter normalization caps dmax. Finish with the existing exact SLSQP constrained polish to convert the near-optimal configuration into a KKT point of the true problem.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: dmin/dmax by maximizing the soft-min distance through potential annealing
tried_paradigms.cautions: Rescale after each step to keep dmax = 1, otherwise all points drift outward; use many random seeds and keep the best; guard against zero distances with a small epsilon; the final SLSQP polish is essential because pure repulsion balances all forces rather than maximizing the true min distance.
